# F15: The metric library on a phone: the first metric near the top, rows of at most three lines, a metric’s goals as rows, nothing scrolls sideways

A check of the Metric library module ([its section](../README.md#journeys-and-checks)): not a journey with steps a person takes, but a script that opens pages and reports what is wrong (Faro’s `evals/finish/15-metrics.cjs`). A rebuild proves the same by hand or with its own script: every failure below must not happen. Each is in the script’s words; {…} is what it measured, and a limit its words don’t give is added after it, in the script’s test (“its test: …”).

## What it checks

the metric library on a phone (ML1, docs/design/metrics/spec.md section 6). run({ open }) returns a list of failures. At 390 px, as a member: the first metric on the library is within 300 px of the top; a row is at most three lines (a long name may take one more); a metric's goals are rows of their own, not a table that scrolls sideways; and nothing on the library, a metric, the form, or the pages the module adds to scrolls sideways. ("Measured by" found by typing, and its sheet's first result, come with ML2.)

## Where it looks

- 390 × 844, as oskar, at `/metrics`, on a touch screen

A width of 390 is a phone, 1440 (or 1280) a desktop; the address is in the demo on Thursday 5 November 2026 unless it names another day. {…} is a value the script works out as it runs.

## What it reports as wrong

- 390px: the first metric on the library is {first}px from the top (at most 300)
- 390px: library rows over three lines: {tall.map((r) => `${r.name} (${r.lines})`).join(', ')}
- 390px: a library row has a button in it
- 390px: a metric’s goals are table rows (display {table.display}), not rows of their own
- 390px: a metric’s goals scroll sideways by {table.wide}px (its test: `table.wide > 1`)
- 390px: scrolls sideways: {sideways.join(', ')}
